sources_read: .qc-cache/coldwater-strict-2026-10-02-r2/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx (Quality Checks row 15 = check 14; Internal Quality Checks row 15 annotations)
evidence: The only shipped data file is task/environment/assets/seed_data.json (149 bytes, LF, ASCII). It parses as JSON: {"snippets": [], "note": "No saved snippets are supplied in this seed. Build a JavaScript and HTML playground with durable revision history."} (seed_data.json:2-3). There are no rows, so no ids, foreign references or orphans are possible; no people, organisations, credentials or secrets; the single free-text note is a plain scope statement consistent with the brief, not an injection payload. It agrees with instruction.md:3 ('/assets/seed_data.json describes the starting scope; there is no starter app to finish') and integration.md:7 ('contains no user snippets or starter implementation'), and with tests/app_context.md:21, which does not assume an empty or pre-populated library. No CSV/TSV, no shipped .db file, and the golden server.js does not insert seeded rows, so there is no second data source to contradict it. A grep of environment/, solve.sh and the golden source for emails, API keys and passwords found only the placeholder git identity turing@local.invalid at environment/Dockerfile:20 (reserved .invalid domain, not personal data). Broken-app probe: an app that ignores the seed loses nothing, since the seed carries no graded figures; conforming-alternative probe: an app that reads the seed and starts with an empty library is not penalised. This row is a static property of the files; no runtime measurement is required for it.
